lines.say: For most lifts, full range of motion builds as much muscle as half reps, or more.
Newer research shows the stretched part matters most. When the muscle is long and loaded, it grows well.
So half reps at the bottom, in the stretch, can work about as well as full reps. Half reps at the top grow the least.
Tiny quick reps at the top, just to move more weight, mostly feed your ego.
Best plan: use full range most of the time. Add stretched half reps at the end of a set if you want.
And control the weight on the way down.
Next: how long until you see results?
